structured_output.hypothesis: Oceanic islands, though poor in species for their area, have a much higher proportion of endemic species in their native floras than similarly sized mainland regions.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using native vascular plant checklists for oceanic (volcanic or never-continental) islands, the median endemic proportion (endemic native species / all native species) is at least 0.20. It is also at least 3 times the median for mainland regions in the same log10-area bins. In addition, median native richness on those islands is below the area-matched mainland median, and at least 25% of the islands have an endemic proportion of 0.30 or more.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The median endemic proportion on oceanic islands is below 0.10, or it is less than 1.5 times the area-matched mainland median. Either result refutes the claim. A mixed result falls between the pass and fail thresholds, and counts as not confirmed.
structured_output.interpretation: 'Oceanic islands' means islands of volcanic or coral origin that were never joined to a continent. In GIFT this means entities with geo_type Island, filtered by the geology or origin attributes in the island metadata. 'Inhabitants' is restricted to vascular plants, because the dataset covers plants only; this is a modern narrowing, and Darwin's claim also covered animals. 'Endemic' means the species is flagged as endemic to the checklist's reference region. 'Extremely large relative to area' becomes a comparison of endemic proportion with mainland regions in the same area bins. 'Few species' becomes lower native richness than area-matched mainland regions. Darwin's mechanism, that colonists are especially liable to modification, cannot be tested with these data. Only the empirical pattern is tested. Fetch note: the fetch tool returned page content but did not display a numeric HTTP status, so 200 is inferred from the successful retrieval.

dataset.name: GIFT – Global Inventory of Floras and Traits (R package GIFT, CRAN page; GIFT database access)
dataset.publisher: Biodiversity, Macroecology & Biogeography group, University of Göttingen (Weigelt, König, Kreft); package hosted on CRAN
dataset.why_it_fits: GIFT holds native, endemic and naturalized plant checklists for about 2,900 regions. These include islands and mainland units with area, so endemic proportion can be compared with mainland regions in the same area bins. The GIFT R package retrieves checklists through the GIFT API. Fields to use are floristic_group (native or endemic), geo_type (Island or Mainland), the entity area, and island geology or origin. The CRAN page confirms the package and API exist. It does not itself show the endemic or island filters, which come from the package documentation.
